reviewer.name: Codex independent review: accuracy and next-action relevance

scope: Evidence review of the unchanged visible October15 article and all three next-action suggestions. Ten confirmed article errors and one unverified claim; supporting API/docs gaps and a per-action usefulness assessment are in the full record. Two independent Codex tasks plus publishing-session integration; same model family, not cross-model assurance. Human disposition remains open. This does not certify producers, deployment, the operating loop or action completion.

findings.title: The identity recommendation reopens an accepted bounded decision
findings.explanation: The exact bounded contract was accepted in Decision16 before the article, with separate publication Decisions17/18. It is closed over Dolt/handoff variants, explicitly excludes universal provider identity, keeps credentials/principals/device metadata out of keys, defines account-independent future GitHub resource identity and fails unsupported GitHub observations closed. Issue57 itself offers a black-box path and conditions its #56 prerequisite on universal-key or client mutation-routing intent. An open issue does not erase the accepted bounded disposition or establish a gate on every inspector feature.
findings.correction: The Dolt/handoff identity boundary is accepted. Keep issue57 for remaining GitHub/provenance decisions; define the source-specific GitHub contract before emitting GitHub records. Apply remaining gates only when the next feature crosses them.

findings.title: Unknown-target rendering is already implemented
findings.explanation: Accepted implementation already renders diagnostic reason labels, literal declared-link status and invalid-declaration reasons, unknown repository text, unavailable source reasons and unavailable process identity. Issue57 covers identity and production provenance, not a generic unresolved badge/style decision. A different visual treatment could be proposed, but the present rendering is not absent.
findings.correction: Describe the implemented explicit diagnostic/status labels and disclosures. Treat any visual refinement as optional UX work rather than a prerequisite attributed to issue57.

findings.title: Four source links miss their intended PRs
findings.explanation: The three shipment headings embed a full PR URL after /pull/, producing malformed destinations. The inline #537 dependency under morning-cockpit points at morning-cockpit/pull/537 rather than core/pull/537. This is one source-link construction finding, not four separate findings.
findings.correction: Use core/pull/537 for the core heading and dependency, morning-cockpit/pull/56 for the cockpit heading, and daily-logger/pull/359 for the logger heading.

findings.title: The refresh repair names the wrong commit
findings.explanation: The full accepted fa5d665 diff is a REST-only claim-routing change. It changes briefing routing and claim eligibility, not inspector detail/refresh request lifetimes. The accepted f47d4c2 commit adds useEvidenceInspector and the request-lifetime controls; the final accepted hook aborts obsolete requests and checks an epoch/detail generation before adopting results.
findings.correction: Attribute the inspector request-lifetime repair to f47d4c2 and the final accepted hook, or omit the single-commit attribution.

findings.title: The product commit count includes the logger article
findings.explanation: The accepted main-history population contains 11 morning-cockpit commits and 3 core commits in the anchored activity window. Fifteen is the total only after adding daily-logger’s one October 14 article commit. The article itself lists the same 11 + 3 + 1 commits.
findings.correction: Say fourteen commits across morning-cockpit and core, or fifteen across all three named repositories.

findings.title: The merges were six hours apart, not fourteen minutes
findings.explanation: Core #537 merged at 2026-10-14T15:15:05Z and morning-cockpit #56 at 2026-10-14T21:40:31Z. Their exact interval is 6 hours, 25 minutes, 26 seconds. Both timestamps were already settled before generation.
findings.correction: Replace fourteen minutes with about six hours and twenty-five minutes, preserving the merge order.

findings.title: The fleet-runner tracker was filed in August
findings.explanation: Core #307 was created on 2026-08-01T12:46:36Z. Its accepted succession/placement decision is dated October 1. October 14 activity added an accepted-reader/operating-boundary update to the existing tracker; it did not create the tracker.
findings.correction: Describe #307 as the existing tracker, originally filed August 1 and repurposed for fleet-runner under the October 1 succession decision.

findings.title: The LEGO correspondence landed October 14
findings.explanation: LEGO PR #47 was created October 14 at 01:28:46Z and merged October 14 at 05:21:37Z. It was already merged before this article generated, but its merge precedes the nominal October 14 09:00Z collection start. That boundary explains exclusion from the day’s three-merge total; it does not make the landing last week.
findings.correction: Say it landed early October 14, outside this article’s anchored activity window.

findings.title: The draft PRs already describe conditional exit paths
findings.explanation: The full PR bodies supply concrete conditional paths. #44 and #46 explicitly say to close or supersede the review draft rather than merge it and state the requirements for a later operative import. #45 states that a second steward still needs to rerun the finalization check before merge, with James controlling merge. None of these receipts supplies a calendar close date, but the blanket no-path assertion is too strong.
findings.correction: Preserve the do-not-merge status and existing close-or-supersede instructions for #44 and #46. State #45's pending second-steward check and owner-controlled merge path. Keep the lack of calendar close dates explicit.

findings.title: Three suggestions follow a two-action introduction
findings.explanation: The Suggested actions block contains three source suggestions. The orientation recommendation is missing from the preceding count/prioritization.
findings.correction: Say three suggested actions, or explicitly distinguish two main priorities and an optional documentation follow-up.

findings.title: The first-maintenance claim is not established
findings.explanation: The byte-equality gate and CI wiring were introduced June27. The October14 accepted-candidate CI has a successful drift-gate step, and acceptance receipts include byte comparisons and distinct actual-schema mutation probes. Those historical schema probes are not automatically evidence of the exact single-byte vendor negative check. No exhaustive maintenance history was found to establish the word first. The narrow negative case is now directly reproduced locally by this review.
findings.correction: Call this a repeatable maintenance replay, cite existing CI/acceptance evidence, and qualify exactly what was tested. Do not describe the pattern or baseline as previously unvalidated.
